header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Amir Hassan (CTO, Solstice AI), Rosa Martinez (Head of Infra, Solstice AI), Liam O'Neill (Security Engineer, Solstice AI)
summary: Discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment options. Customer evaluating private VPC peering vs private endpoints, region constraints, CIDR overlap, transit gateway options, and KMS/HSM integration. Agreement to share security docs, architecture diagram, and schedule deep technical walkthrough week of 2026-07-27.
topics: KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Ethan from Redwood, I have Maya with me from our SE team.
[00:08] Amir: Hey, thanks, Ethan. Amir here. Short on time, so appreciate keeping to a tight agenda.
[00:12] Rosa: Hi all. Rosa on infra. We have a few network folks on standby.
[00:16] Liam: Liam from security, quick background on compliance.
[00:19] Maya: Great—today we'll focus on Private deployment networking, VPC peering, private endpoints, and region constraints. We'll also cover key security integrations.
[00:28] Ethan: Quick qual—what's your current stack? Are you on AWS, GCP, multi-cloud?
[00:33] Amir: Primarily AWS, us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for now, planning ap-southeast-1 later this year.
[00:39] Rosa: We're using multiple accounts per team, central transit gateway for egress policies.
[00:44] Ethan: Good. For Redwood Private, we support both VPC peering and private endpoints. Maya can walk through tradeoffs.
[00:52] Maya: Yeah so, peering is straightforward for low latency—it's classic VPC to VPC. Private endpoints (like privatelink) are an option if you want cross-account private connectivity without full route exposure. Keep in mind CIDR overlap, and peering won't route through a transit gw if you need it to, so depends on your architecture.
[01:15] Rosa: CIDR overlap is a big one for us, we have many /16s in the org. Does Redwood support transitive peering via a transit gateway?
[01:23] Maya: We don't terminate into customers' transit gateway directly by default; typical pattern is VPC peering or private endpoint into a customer-managed VPC. For transit gw scenarios we can discuss a dedicated arrangement—some customers set up a small relay VPC.
[01:36] Liam: On the security side: we need static egress IPs for firewall allowlists. Can you provide fixed egress IPs for outbound calls from the model infra?
[01:45] Ethan: Yes, we can provide egress IPs per region for Private deployments; for Hosted it's different. For Private we can either have the deployment inside your VPC (private subnets) or peer into ours and provide dedicated egress ranges.
[01:58] Amir: If we do peering, who manages NAT/egress? We prefer keeping control in our account.
[02:05] Maya: If the model runs in Redwood-managed VPC and you peer, we can configure NAT on our side and provide stable egress. Alternatively, for full control you deploy Redwood Private into your VPC (customer-managed)—that gives you total control but requires more infra on your end.
[02:22] Rosa: Can you expand on the "deploy into our VPC" option—does that need on-prem or just cloud?
[02:28] Maya: Cloud VPC deployment is the common approach—Redwood Private components (control plane or data plane depending on model) can be packaged to run in your account. We have a private control plane option and an on-prem package. The cloud VPC option keeps data in your network and keys in your KMS.
[02:44] Liam: KMS integration—do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed keys?
[02:49] Maya: Yes, we integrate with KMS in AWS and customer-provided HSM via supported providers. We'll detail recommended key rotation and envelope encryption patterns in the security package.
[02:59] Amir: Region constraints—we want model endpoints in eu-west-1 for data residency. Can you guarantee single-region deployment?
[03:07] Ethan: Yes, you can pin deployments to specific regions. For HA across regions we recommend active-passive with failover, but multi-region active is more complex because of KV cache sync. We'll share notes on tradeoffs.
[03:20] Rosa: About model updates—if you pin a model version, can we control rollouts?
[03:24] Maya: Absolutely—Redwood supports rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to smaller/cheaper variants. That works similarly in Private deployments; you control model versioning through the same API.
[03:34] Amir: One concern—latency. If we run in a different region than our users, will that add latency?
[03:40] Maya: Latency is driven by where the model runs relative to your client traffic. If you need low tail latency for EU users, run the inference in eu-west-1. Also batching behavior can impact median latency versus p99.
[03:50] Rosa: Do you have recommended CIDR ranges for the Redwood side to avoid conflict?
[03:54] Maya: We usually recommend non-overlapping /24s or /20s depending on scale. We'll send a sample list. Also if you use AWS Transit Gateway, you'll need to ensure route propagation settings don't create loops.
[04:08] Liam: Audit logs—we need immutable audit trails for model requests and key usage. How granular are your audit logs?
[04:15] Maya: We surface per-request metadata, model/version, timestamps, request IDs, and anonymized content options. For Private we can push logs to your CloudWatch/S3 with lifecycle policies. If you need more granular traces, we can enable additional retention but that has cost implications.
[04:32] Amir: Does Redwood support SAML/SSO and RBAC integration with our identity provider?
[04:36] Ethan: Yes, we support SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC. For Private deployments, you can connect to your IdP and manage roles via your existing systems.
[04:45] Rosa: Network route—are we talking peering (V P C) or endpoint (privatelink)? Could you summarize when to pick which?
[04:52] Maya: Sure—peering is good for low-latency full VPC connectivity when CIDRs don't overlap; it's simple and fast. Private endpoints are better for cross-account access with minimal routing exposure and when you want to avoid route table complexity. If you need NAT/control in your account, deploy into your VPC.
[05:10] Amir: Do you support AWS PrivateLink for model inference traffic?
[05:13] Maya: We can expose a PrivateLink endpoint for the control plane or API; for token streaming and high-throughput model inference it's less common but possible—we'll scope bandwidth considerations.
[05:24] Ethan: A practical note—some customers prefer peering for simplicity for POCs, then move to endpoints or in-VPC model for production.
[05:33] Rosa: What about cross-region peering? We have infra in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
[05:38] Maya: Cross-region peering is supported but increases latency and egress costs. For best performance keep inference in the region closest to users. For failover we use cross-region backups.
[05:48] Liam: Compliance question—do you sign BAA or handle PHI?
[05:52] Ethan: We have enterprise plans with compliances; for PHI we'd discuss legal and a BAA. We'll include that in the security packet.
[05:59] Amir: Can you give an example network diagram for peering?
[06:03] Maya: Yes, we'll attach a diagram showing Redwood VPC <-> Customer VPC peering, route tables, security groups, and CIDR examples.
[06:12] Rosa: Is there any requirement for a bastion or jump host for management?
[06:16] Maya: Typically management is via the control plane APIs and console; for customer-managed deployments you may have a bastion for admin access. For Redwood-managed we handle maintenance and expose ops endpoints to your network on request.
[06:30] Amir: Latency numbers—do you have p99 or throughput benchmarks for the models?
[06:35] Ethan: We maintain perf profiles per model. We'll share Redwood-verified benchmarks (median and p99) for the models you're evaluating. For Private deployments numbers are similar if the infra is comparable.
[06:48] Ros: (sic) sorry, Rosa: Any limits on connection count or concurrent streams?
[06:52] Maya: We support streaming and can scale capacity; Dedicated capacity reservations help guarantee concurrency. We'll propose a sizing based on your expected RPS and concurrency.
[07:05] Amir: On cost—how do pricing models differ between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private?
[07:09] Ethan: Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with monthly commits. Private has enterprise licensing and may include infra pass-through or a platform fee. We'll send a pricing summary.
[07:18] Liam: For network ACLs and security groups, will we see source IPs for each request?
[07:23] Maya: Yes, you'll see client source IPs in flow logs if you deploy in your VPC; with peering we can provide connection metadata and flow logs mapped to request IDs.
[07:34] Rosa: What about multi-tenant risk—if Redwood manages infra in your VPC, do you still have tenant isolation?
[07:40] Maya: In customer-managed VPCs you control tenancy. In Redwood-managed deployments we ensure workload isolation with dedicated namespaces and IAM, but customer-managed is the strongest isolation model.
[07:53] Amir: Can Redwood integrate with our existing monitoring (DataDog / Prometheus)?
[07:58] Ethan: Yes, we can export metrics to your monitoring endpoints and integrate with tracing. We'll put examples in the tech pack.
[08:08] Rosa: Any gotchas for AWS PrivateLink and cross-account endpoints?
[08:13] Maya: PrivateLink requires accepting endpoint services and has quotas per region; it avoids route table changes but has per-GB costs. We'll outline tradeoffs.
[08:25] Liam: Quick on encryption in transit—TLS mutual auth or simple TLS?
[08:29] Maya: We support mTLS for service-to-service and can require client certs for sensitive connections in Private deployments.
[08:36] Ethan: Want to cover timeline—what's your target for a POC?
[08:40] Amir: Ideally next month, POC in eu-west-1, 2-week pilot to validate latency and data residency.
[08:46] Ethan: That sounds good. We'll scope a small pilot with peering first and then propose options for in-VPC for production.
[08:52] Rosa: For the peering we need a checklist—CIDR, routes, security groups, NACLs, accepted peering, and test plan.
[08:59] Maya: We'll send a checklist and a runbook for smoke tests (small sample workloads, latency/throughput tests, and logging validation).
[09:09] Amir: Any legal requirements for cross-border data transfer if we keep logs?
[09:13] Liam: We'll need data residency assurances; if logs leave region we need controls.
[09:18] Ethan: For Private in-region deployments, logs can be stored in-region into your S3/CloudWatch. We'll document retention and anonymization capabilities.
[09:27] Rosa: One more—how are upgrades/patches handled for private infra?
[09:31] Maya: For customer-managed we provide upgrade scripts and can schedule maintenance windows. For Redwood-managed we coordinate upgrades and provide rollback options.
[09:40] Amir: Ok good. Can you send the security pack and sample pricing, and we'll align on a date for the deep dive?
[09:46] Ethan: Yes—Ethan to send security pack and architecture diagram tomorrow. Maya will schedule the infra deep dive for the week of 7/27.
[09:54] Liam: We'll send our CIDR ranges and a list of required IP allowlists by Friday.
[09:59] Rosa: And we'll pull in our network engineer for the next call.
[10:03] Ethan: Perfect. Recap: security docs + diagram, pricing summary, VPC peering checklist, schedule deep dive. Anything else?
[10:12] Amir: No that's it, thanks.
[10:16] Ethan: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
[10:20] TRANSCRIPT NOTES: occasional mis-hearings and filler words present; some speaker labels simplified.
